original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dgen(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in general position, meaning no three points are collinear and no four points are cocircular.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 8 in the current arXiv version of the survey (the same statement appears as Problem 11 in the June 2014 PDF): determine the asymptotic value of D_gen(n) for n-point planar sets in general position.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it asks for the asymptotic value of D_gen(n), keeps the setting planar, and uses the paper's general-position condition that no three points are collinear and no four are cocircular. It also correctly treats D_gen(n) as a minimum over n-point sets, rather than a pinned, bipartite, convex-position, or no-parallelogram variant.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane R^2.
The distance notion should be stated explicitly as ordinary Euclidean distance between pairs of distinct points.
D_gen(n) should be defined formally as a minimum over all finite sets P subset R^2 with |P| = n satisfying the general-position condition.
To make 'asymptotic value' fully stand-alone, it helps to say that the problem asks for the growth rate of D_gen(n) as n tends to infinity, i.e. up to asymptotic order.
refined_question: Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of distinct points of a finite set P subset R^2. Define D_gen(n) := min { D(P) : P subset R^2, |P| = n, no three points of P are collinear, and no circle contains four points of P }. Determine the asymptotic growth of D_gen(n) as n -> infinity.
justification: This is the exact open problem stated in the paper for planar sets in general position. The introduction defines D(P), and Section 3 then defines general position as 'no three points are collinear and no four points are cocircular,' introduces D_gen(n) as the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point set with that property, and immediately asks for its asymptotic value. The nearby context adds only orientation—namely, that the convex n-gon is not in general position, that it is unknown whether D_gen(n) = Theta(n), and that the best known upper and trivial lower bounds come from earlier work—so the paper-faithful refinement should stay exactly with this asymptotic D_gen(n) question.
